brief: A kitchen herb planter: two or three bins on a base, filled with soil and planted with basil and thyme.

requirements.evidence: Three base pieces with bins, soil and plants, check_build clear.

requirements.requirement: Two or three bins on a base
requirements.evidence: Three hex-bin-full-drain-pill bins at bin:0,0,0, bin:0,1,0, bin:1,0,0 on the base pieces.
fillSoil applied to all three bins.
basil-young in bins at 0,0 and 1,0; thyme-young in bin at 0,1.

requirements.requirement: Suitable for kitchen use (food-safe, water, washable material)
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit and collisions only; material and food safety are not verified.

finish.summary: Built a three-cell herb planter: three adjacent base pieces (one at 0,0; two added at 1,0 and 0,1) joined by locked joint bolts, each carrying a full-depth drained bin with pill holes filled with soil. Basil (young) is in the bins at 0,0 and 1,0, thyme (young) in the bin at 0,1. Open faces are capped and the check reports no issues and a clear mesh. Material suitability for kitchen use (food safety, water, dishwashing) is not something the configurator checks, so that is not verified.

lines.label: Bin, full depth, drained, pill holes
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
